messages.author: cbb14406dcfff2da
messages.subject: geom_segment
parts:
Hi, love Deducer, wondering whether geom_segment will be added to the
list of Geometric Elements to choose from in Plot Builder or if there
is a way to add it manually and reintroduce through a template?

Thanks
Gerry

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: geom_segment
parts:
Gerry,

There are ways to manually add new geoms/stats to the builder (without
even leaving R:
http://www.youtube.com/user/MrIanfellows#p/u/0/RsxOo0jx0II ), but the
omission of segment is an oversight. I also noticed that rug is
missing too.

I've added both of these into the development version. you can install it with

install.packages('Deducer',,'http://www.rforge.net/',type='source')

provided you can install source packages. I've attached two example
plots with the new geoms.

Cheers,
Ian

> list of Geometric Elements to choose from in Plot Builder or if there
> is a way to add it manually and reintroduce through a template?
>
> Thanks
> Gerry

messages.author: cbb14406dcfff2da
messages.subject: Re: geom_segment
parts:
Thanks again Ian, however I now have some follow ups( that'll teach you for being so efficient!!

1. I installed the development version on a Mac OS/X latest version ( and the Patched Mac R mentioned in the next post) and the rug and segment geoms appear and work Excellent.
I then installed on my laptop running Ubuntu 11.04 . Compiled with no errors, but I can't see the new geoms on the ubuntu system.

2. I'm using deducer because I'm hoping it will break my wifes dependency on me doing her stats work! (hers is the Mac, mines the ubuntu system) . I'm trying to recreate this plot in deducer which I've written in ggplot2. 

#******************Bland Altman Transform and Plots for Peak Flow vs Predicted PF *****#
require(ggplot2)
pfd <- subset(Pdata, select=c(Peak.Fl,Pred.PF))
pfd <- na.omit(pfd)

pfd <- transform(pfd, FlPFmean = (Peak.Fl + Pred.PF)/2)
pfd <- transform(pfd, diff = (Peak.Fl - Pred.PF))

#dev.new()
ggplot() +
geom_hline(data=pfd,aes(yintercept=mean(diff)),linetype = "dotted") +
        geom_hline(data=pfd,aes(yintercept= 0),,linetype = "solid") +
geom_hline(data=pfd,aes(yintercept=mean(diff)-c(-2,2)*sd(diff)),linetype = "dotdash" ) +
        geom_point(aes(x = FlPFmean,y = diff),data=pfd, colour = "steelblue") +
scale_y_continuous(name = "Difference (Actual - Pred)\n     (l/min)",limits = c(-550,550)) +
scale_x_continuous(name= "Average (Actual + Pred)/2 \n (l/min)", limits= c(200,700))

#****************************************************************



To recreate in Plot Builder, I add 3 hline geoms, the points, and X and Y continuous scales and I was hoping to be able to enter "mean(diff)" and "mean(diff)-c(-2,2)*sd(diff)" into the Y intercept box, but when I view the call, these statements are enclosed within inverted commas and do not evaluate when run.  Is there a way to enter functions into the input box so that it writes the call minus the inverted commas (i.e. something like %mean(diff)%  - which I haven't tried......)


The only way I have been able to workaround has been to enter the values manually (which is less than optimal!) I'm sure theres a way to do it, I just haven't been able to find it. I've watched the videos, searched the group , read the wiki manual and package doco.

3. Same question re evaluated statements for the Transform Function - I'd like to be able to do the transforms above within Deducer, but not sure how.

Thanks in advance, cheers
Gerry

The new geoms are only in the development version of Deducer 0.4-5.

> pfd <- transform(pfd, diff = (Peak.Fl - Pred.PF))

> ggplot() +
> geom_hline(data=pfd,aes(yintercept=mean(diff)),linetype = "dotted") +
>         geom_hline(data=pfd,aes(yintercept= 0),,linetype = "solid") +
> geom_hline(data=pfd,aes(yintercept=mean(diff)-c(-2,2)*sd(diff)),linetype =
> "dotdash" ) +
>         geom_point(aes(x = FlPFmean,y = diff),data=pfd, colour =
> "steelblue") +
> scale_y_continuous(name = "Difference (Actual - Pred)\n     (l/min)",limits
> = c(-550,550)) +
> scale_x_continuous(name= "Average (Actual + Pred)/2 \n (l/min)", limits=
> c(200,700))
> #****************************************************************
>
>
> To recreate in Plot Builder, I add 3 hline geoms, the points, and X and Y
> continuous scales and I was hoping to be able to enter "mean(diff)" and
> "mean(diff)-c(-2,2)*sd(diff)" into the Y intercept box, but when I view the
> call, these statements are enclosed within inverted commas and do not
> evaluate when run.  Is there a way to enter functions into the input box so
> that it writes the call minus the inverted commas (i.e. something like
> %mean(diff)%  - which I haven't tried......)

You can right click on the drop field for yintercept, which will allow
you to write in a custom statement.

> 3. Same question re evaluated statements for the Transform Function - I'd
> like to be able to do the transforms above within Deducer, but not sure how.

You can enter custom statements into the Transform Dialog. For
example: mean(x,na.rm=T) - 2*sd(x,na.rm=T)
